title: Dedicated Pool Economics — Q2 Runbook and Autoscale Initiative
creator: Jonah Reinhardt
description: Create a prescriptive Q2 runbook and delivery plan that aligns Dedicated pool sizing, reservation hedging, and autoscale step policies to unit economics targets. This ticket captures the product decisions, rollout milestones, monitoring dashboards, and communication plan for dedicated capacity customers and SRE/TPM adoption. The runbook should be operational (play-by-play) and include rollback criteria, canary profiles, and cross-team responsibilities.
objectives: Reduce 1M-token normalized cost for standard dedicated pools by 12% through smarter autoscale step sizing and short-term reservation hedges
Define and ship versioned autoscale policy templates (latency-first, cost-first, balanced) with clear customer defaults
Deliver an on-call runbook and console UI flows that make pool resizing, hedging, and emergency drain operations executable within 30 minutes
okrs: OKR-1: Cost efficiency — Move unit cost from $8.50 to <= $7.50 per 1M tokens on typical 'balanced' workloads (measured week-over-week)
OKR-2: Reliability — Maintain 99.9% regional uptime for dedicated pools during autoscale events
OKR-3: Adoption — 60% of new Dedicated customers select a managed autoscale template within 7 days of onboarding
roadmap: Phase A (Mar 2026): Analysis and sizing experiments — run 4 pilot reservations and evaluate burst buffer configs
Phase B (Apr 2026): Policy templates + console UX — ship autoscale templates and a simplified 'apply policy' flow
Phase C (May 2026): Observability & Alerts — cost-attribution dashboards, regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets
Phase D (Jun 2026): Canary and rollout — customer canaries, runbook drills, and GA release for reservation hedging
milestones: 2026-03-15: Pilot reservation hedging experiment (complete, see pilot notes)
2026-05-05: Console apply-policy UX beta released to internal accounts
risks: Over-hedging reservation purchases could increase short-term cash outlay and reduce flexibility
Autoscale oscillation under spiky traffic if step sizes are mis-tuned — requires safety cooldowns
Confusing defaults may lead to customer complaints if cost vs latency tradeoffs are not surfaced clearly
stakeholders: Miguel Ortega — Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
metrics: Pool utilization (avg GPU occupancy over 5m windows)
Autoscale success rate (no failed scale operations) >= 99%
Time to mitigate (execute runbook) <= 30 minutes for high-severity incidents
notes: Pilot results showed 9% cost improvement with a 2-week reservation hedge on predictable baseline traffic; engineering flagged potential cache-eviction latency regressions for one model family — decided to scope a hotspot protection patch. PM/Eng review (2026-02-25) preferred conservative defaults for GA: balanced template with small reservation hedges and explicit opt-in for aggressive cost mode.
public_summary: Q2 initiative to align dedicated capacity autoscale policies with clear economic guardrails: ship policy templates, observability, and an operational runbook so customers get predictable performance and cost.
